clauses.label: operative lead
clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in
me by the Constitution and laws of the
United States, including the Defense Pro­
duction Act of 1950, as amended (50
U. S. C. App. 2061 et seq.), hereinafter
referred to as the Act, and as President
of the United States and Commander in
Chief of the armed forces of the United
States, it is ordered that the functions re­
maining under Title IV of the Act shall
be, and they are hereby, delegated as
follows:

clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Fiscal liquidation. Such
functions as remain in connection with
the fiscal liquidation of the Economic
Stabilization Agency are hereby trans­
ferred to the Secretary of the Treasury.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Administrative proceedings.
The function of conducting administra­
tive proceedings under Title IV of the
Act, including the conclusion of those
instituted pursuant to section 405 and
the taking of necessary actions under
sections 407 and 408 of the Act, is hereby
transferred to the Director of the Office
of Defense Mobilization.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Enforcement and investiga­
tions. In addition to the functions now
vested in the Attorney General by the
Act, he shall have, and there are hereby
transferred to him, the following-de­
scribed functions under Title IV of the
Act: (a) completing the processing of
enforcement files, (b) concluding inves­
tigations where deemed appropriate, and

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) certifying disallowances (section
409 (d) >.
Sections 1 and 2 of this order shall be­
come effective November 1, 1953. Sec­
tion 3 shall become effective immediately.

versions.research_rationale: EO 10494 (signed 1953-10-14, 18 FR 6585), read in full from the held official FR text (pdfplumber reading-order recheck of PDF pages 3-4): preamble delegating 'the functions remaining under Title IV' of the Defense Production Act; sec. 1 ESA fiscal liquidation to the Treasury; sec. 2 Title IV administrative proceedings to the ODM Director; sec. 3(a)-(c) enforcement files, investigations and disallowance certification to the Attorney General; last paragraph: secs. 1-2 effective November 1, 1953, sec. 3 immediately. It has no term or sunset. EO 12148 sec. 5-103 revokes it 'as amended', effective 1979-07-15 under EO 12148 sec. 6. The dossier's 5 clauses cover the order from the enacting paragraph to the signature with no textual gap. D6 / earlier-end test: the OFR catalog records amendments by EO 10773 (1958) and EO 11051 (1962), a 'see' note from EO 11725 (1973) and the EO 12148 revocation; the USC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 records the EO 12148 revocation. All three changing orders were read in the held FR texts and are attached as later events on sec. 2, the only clause naming the ODM Director: EO 10773 sec. 3 (ODM to OCDM, 1958-07-01), EO 11051 sec. 601(7) (OCDM to OEP, 1962-09-27) and EO 11725 sec. 3 item (5) (OEP authority under this order to GSA, 1973-07-01). None ends a clause. The OFR edge crediting EO 10494 with revoking EO 10332 is a page-sharing artifact: the revocation of EO 10332 is Part VI of EO 10495, printed next to it on the same page; it is not an act of this order. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12148 (EO 12148, 44 FR 43239-43245, read once in full): sec. 6 makes the order effective July 15, 1979 although it was signed July 20, 1979, so the sec. 5-1 revocations take effect 1979-07-15; sec. 5-1 revokes thirteen orders 'as amended' without exception or delayed effect; the only continuation clause, sec. 2-302, lets the FEMA Director keep performing the functions transferred to him by sec. 1 'notwithstanding the revocations', which preserves FEMA's own transferred functions, not any provision of a revoked order; sec. 1-201 moves records, property, personnel and funds for the sec. 1 functions only. There is no pending-matter or savings clause for the revoked orders. Own-residual check, reading EO 10494 in full: it transferred the remaining Title IV (price and wage stabilization) functions of the Defense Production Act on the wind-down of the Economic Stabilization Agency: ESA fiscal liquidation to the Treasury Secretary (sec. 1), the conduct and conclusion of Title IV administrative proceedings to the ODM Director (sec. 2; later OCDM, OEP and, from 1973, GSA under EO 10773, 11051 and 11725), and the enforcement files, investigations and certification of disallowances to the Attorney General (sec. 3). Liquidation steps taken, proceedings concluded and disallowances certified before 1979-07-15 are completed acts under the transferred functions; EO 12148 does not undo them, and its sec. 2-302 continuation (FEMA's own functions) does not re-enact this order. No clause of EO 10494 continues; state transferred_or_accrued records the completed transfers and their effects. S1 transfer-wording prefill (review) resolved to transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: the order and the ending instrument read in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals, every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

later_events.mechanism: amendment of references, not an end: EO 10773 sec. 3(a)-(b) (signed July 1, 1958, 23 FR 5061; implementing Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958; no separate effective-date wording) amends each reference in any prior Executive order to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization or that Office to refer to the Director of the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization (later Civil and Defense Mobilization); the FR codification table printed with it lists the order as 'amended by EO 10773'. The order list on 23 FR 5063 is not in the held text; the producer relies on the general sec. 3 wording, which reaches this order's ODM reference. It moves no end date

amendment of references, not an end: EO 11051 sec. 601 (signed September 27, 1962, 27 FR 9683; no effective-date wording) amends each reference to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization or its Director in a listed set of orders, including EO 10494 (item 7) and EO 10634 (item 9), to refer to the Office of Emergency Planning and its Director. It moves no end date

transfer of the residual authority, not an end: EO 11725 sec. 3 (signed June 27, 1973, 38 FR 17175; 'effective as of July 1, 1973' by sec. 8) transfers all authority vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness by Executive order, other than disaster relief and import investigations, to the Administrator of General Services, naming among those functions EO 10494 (item 5) and EO 10634 (item 7); its sec. 4 continues existing actions. It changes the officer, not the life of the clause; EO 12148 sec. 5-112 later revoked EO 11725 too
